A.text: In an experiment, brass and steel wires of length 1 m each with areas of cross section 1 mm² are used. The wires are connected in series and one end of the combined wire is connected to a rigid support and other end is subjected to elongation. The stress required to produce a net elongation of 0.2 mm is, [Given, the Young's Modulus for steel and brass are, respectively, 120 × 10⁹ N/m² and 60 × 10⁹ N/m²]

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A tube of length H is open at one end. It is lowered into a tank of mercury as shown in figure with open end downward. The closed end is just on the surface. The mercury is pushed into the tube to a height h. If the atmosphere pressure is H of mercury, then choose correct relation. Neglect surface tension
A.sol_text:
Answer : (2)
Solution:
P₀AH = P₁A(H - h), where P₁ is the pressure of air column trapped in the tube.
P₁ = (P₀H)/(H - h)
Also P₁ = P₀ + (H - h)
P₁ = 2H - h
⇒ (H²)/(H - h) + h = 2H
⇒ (2H - h)(H - h) = H²

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A diatomic ideal gas expands from volume V₀ to 2V₀ as shown in indicator diagram. For this process, the correct statement is
options: Specific heat of the gas is positive throughout the process
Specific heat of the gas is negative throughout the process
Specific heat of the gas is negative from V = 3V₀/2 to V = 7V₀/4
Specific heat of the gas is negative from V = 5V₀/4 to V = 3V₀/2
A.sol_text:
P = -(P₀/V₀)V + 3P₀

⇒ nRT/V = -(P₀/V₀)V + 3P₀

⇒ nRT = -(P₀/V₀)V² + 3P₀V ... (i)

When system starts rejecting heat
dQ < 0
⇒ dU + dW < 0
⇒ (5/2)nR(dT/dV) + P < 0 ... (ii)

From equation (i)
(5/2)[3P₀ - (2P₀V/V₀)] + [3P₀ - (P₀V/V₀)] < 0

On solving V > 7V₀/4

When volume of gas lies between 7V₀/4 to 2V₀, then gas rejects heat.

Maximum value of temperature occurs at
V = (3/2)V₀, because from equation (i)
dT/dV = 0 ⇒ V = (3/2)V₀

Temperature increases from A to B and decreases from B to D.
In region B → C, ΔQ → (-)ve, ΔT → (-)ve
∴ Specific heat capacity is (-)ve in region B → C.

A.text: The pressure of one mole of an ideal gas varies according to the equation P = P₀ - aV², where P₀ and a are positive constants. The maximum temperature attained by the gas during the process is
A.sol_text:

(P₀ - aV²)V = nRT
On differentiation, we get
(P₀ - 3aV²) = nR(dT)/(dV)
(dT)/(dV) = 0 & (d²T)/(dV²) = -ve
0 = (dT)/(dV) ⇒ 3aV² = P₀ or V = √(P₀/(3a))
∴ T_max = (2P₀)/(3R) √(P₀/(3a))

A.text: A large tank of cross-section area A contains liquid of density ρ. A cylinder of density (ρ/4) and length l and cross-section area a (a << A) is kept in equilibrium by applying an external vertically downward force as shown. The cylinder is just submerged in liquid. At t = 0 the external force is removed instantaneously. Assume that water level in the tank remains constant. The velocity of the cylinder when it reaches its equilibrium position is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (4)
Hint:
V = Aω
Solution:
The density of liquid is four times that of cylinder, hence in equilibrium position one fourth of the cylinder will remain submerged. So as the cylinder is released from initial position it moves distance (3l/4) to reach its equilibrium position. The upward motion in this duration is SHM.
Therefore attained velocity is V_max = Aω

where, ω = √(4g/l) and A = 3l/4
Thus, V_max = (3/2)√(gl)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A block of mass m is suspended vertically by a spring of spring constant k. It is released from rest at t = 0 from unstretched position of the spring. The time instant when speed of block becomes v first time is
A.sol_text:
The block performs SHM
∴ y = A cosωt, ω = √(k/m)
∴ v = ωA sinωt, A = mg/k
∴ v = √(k/m) × (mg/k) sin(√(k/m) t)
∴ t = √(m/k) sin⁻¹(√(k/m) v/(mg))

Alternatively:
∴ t = √(m/k) sin⁻¹(√(k·v)/(m·g))

A.text: Vibrating tuning fork of frequency n is placed near the open end of a long cylindrical tube. The tube has a side opening and is fitted with a movable reflecting piston. A.sol_text:

So, v = nλ ⟹ n = v/λ = 350/0.35 = 1000 Hz

A.text:
In the following question more than one correlation is possible between options of Column-I and Column-II. Make as many correlations as you can.
Match the ions given in Column-I with their nature given in Column-II

Which of the following options contain the correct match?

(1) (i)-(C); (ii)-(D); (iii)-(C); (iv)-(A)
(2) (i)-(C); (ii)-(A); (iii)-(A); (iv)-(B)
(3) (i)-(A, B); (ii)-(B); (iii)-(B); (iv)-(C, D)
(4) (i)-(C, D); (ii)-(C); (iii)-(D); (iv)-(A, B)
A.sol_text:
Answer : (3)
Solution:

CH₃ - O⁺ = CH - CH₃ ⇌ CH₃ - O = CH - CH₃
        ↑                    ⊕

Stabilise due to resonance and also destabilise due to –I effect of O atom but stabilising effect dominates.

(i) CH₃ - O - CH - CH₃: (A) Stable due to resonance; (B) Destabilised due to inductive effect
(ii) CF₃ - CH₂⁺: (B) Destabilised due to inductive effect
(iii) CH₃ - C⊖ with CH₃ and CH₃ attached: (B) Destabilised due to inductive effect
(iv) CH₃ - CH - CH₃ with ⊕: (C) Stabilised by hyperconjugation; (D) A secondary carbocation (A secondary carbon attached with two other carbons)
